questions.feedback: That trap answer is the one to unlearn: The flower is the end of the life of the plant. Reteach point: The flower is not the end: inside the flower new seeds are forming, and the cycle starts again. Check scene s2: look inside the flower and watch the new seeds forming.
questions.misconception: The flower is the end of the life of the plant.
questions.prompt: Why is the flower NOT the end of the life of the plant?

questions.feedback: Scenes s3 and s4 fix the order: the egg hatches into a caterpillar, the caterpillar changes inside a pupa, and an adult butterfly emerges.
questions.prompt: Name, in order, the four stages of a butterfly's life cycle.

questions.feedback: Scene s1 fixes the picture: the seed wakes up and sprouts a root and a shoot, becoming a seedling - the baby plant.
questions.prompt: What does a seed become right after it sprouts?

questions.answer: It lays eggs on a leaf, and the eggs hatch into caterpillars.
questions.feedback: Scene s4 fixes the loop: the adult butterfly lays eggs, so the cycle starts all over again - egg to caterpillar to pupa to butterfly.
questions.prompt: After an adult butterfly emerges from its pupa, what does it do that starts the cycle again?
